items.title: City of Edmonton Bylaw 18155, Council Procedures Bylaw (consolidated October 29, 2025), s.38

citations.finding: The standing limit for each approved speaker is 5 minutes. Section 38 was last amended by Bylaw 20226 (2022-07-04), and none of the later listed amendments (Bylaws 20868, 21303, 21365) is noted against section 38.
citations.establishes: The standing per-speaker limit in force as of the consolidation date was 5 minutes.
citations.quote: Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes.

citations.finding: A Standing Committee may waive or modify any part of the bylaw by special resolution, which is defined as at least two-thirds of all members of the Standing Committee voting in favour.
citations.establishes: The kind of vote needed for a committee to change the s.38 limits for a meeting.
citations.quote: Council or a Standing Committee may waive or modify the application of any part of this bylaw by special resolution

citations.finding: Section 38(1) sets a maximum of five minutes for each approved speaker. Section 4 allows a Standing Committee to modify the bylaw by special resolution; section 2 defines that as at least two-thirds of all committee members voting in favour.
citations.establishes: The standing speaking limit and the procedure and threshold for modifying it.
citations.quote: Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes.

citations.finding: Section 38(1) says each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of five minutes. Sections 2(m) and 4 require at least two-thirds of all committee members to vote for a modification. The consolidation's amendment list ends October 29, 2025; a search of the City's bylaw index on October 2, 2026 identified no later amendment to section 38.
citations.establishes: The standing five-minute maximum and the special-resolution threshold.
citations.quote: Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes.

items.title: Infrastructure Committee, August 26, 2026, post-meeting minutes, item 1.4
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Office of the City Clerk

citations.finding: Under item 1.4, M. Janz moved that the Infrastructure Committee adjust the s.38 time limits for the 2026-08-26 meeting so that each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes, and members of Council get three minutes to ask questions and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion. All six members voted in favour; carried 6 to 0.
citations.establishes: The committee carried a motion cutting the per-speaker maximum from 5 to 3 minutes for every approved speaker at that meeting, by a vote that meets the special-resolution threshold on the minutes' attendance.
citations.quote: each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes

citations.finding: The item 2.3 Requests to Speak motion (A. Salvador, carried 6 to 0) lists 64 entries for item 7.6 in five panels (15, 15, 15, 15, 4), 15 of them with an organization's name. The whole list across four items totals 78, plus 1 additional speaker on item 7.4, so N-all = 79.
citations.establishes: Primary count N = 64 approved-speaker entries on item 7.6, inside the 60-80 band (reviewer's count of entries).

citations.finding: Item 2.4 set item 7.6 as the first item of business, so the item 1.4 time-limit motion came before any public speaker on the bike-lane item.
citations.establishes: The 3-minute limit was in place before the bike-lane speakers were heard.
citations.quote: 7.6 Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration Program Update - First item of business

citations.finding: The item 7.6 presentation lists record 52 entries as having presented (panels 16, 16, 18, 2), 12 of them with an organization's name. That is below the 60-80 primary band, though inside 50-90.
citations.establishes: If 'the queue' means people who actually spoke on the item, the 'about seventy' figure falls outside the primary band. This makes the finding definition-sensitive (reviewer's count of entries).

citations.finding: Under item 1.4, Councillor M. Janz moved to adjust section 38 for the 2026-08-26 meeting so each approved speaker could speak for a maximum of three minutes and each Council member had three minutes to ask questions and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion. All six members voted in favour; it carried 6 to 0. The six votes meet the four-vote minimum required by the bylaw's two-thirds-of-all-members rule.
citations.establishes: The carried three-minute limit, its coverage, mover, vote and result.
citations.quote: each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes

citations.finding: Item 2.3 lists five panels approved for item 7.6, with 15, 15, 15, 15 and 4 entries respectively: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 + 4 = 64 entries (reviewer's calculation). Fourteen entries carry organization names. The organizations are Edmonton Bike Coalition; YEG Bike Coalition; Bike Bus Alberta; Holyrood Voice; Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group; Paths for People; Ward Métis Bikes; Let's Bike There YEG; and Bike Edmonton.
citations.establishes: The primary approved-speaker count is 64 entries, within the 60–80 band.

citations.finding: The item 7.6 presentation lists contain 16, 16, 18 and 2 entries by panel, totaling 52 (reviewer's calculation). Twelve entries carry an organization name. This count is below the primary 60–80 band if the holder's queue figure is interpreted as people who actually presented rather than people approved to speak.
citations.establishes: The recorded presentation count is 52 entries, below the primary magnitude band; it does not disprove the approved-list count of 64.

citations.finding: Counting all approved entries across the four items gives 79: item 7.1 has 5, item 7.3 has 1, item 7.4 has 9 including the additional speaker, and item 7.6 has 64. This alternative remains within both magnitude bands but is not the primary item 7.6 count.
citations.establishes: The alternative whole-meeting count is 79 entries; it does not alter the item 7.6 primary count.

citations.finding: Under item 1.4, M. Janz moved a section 38 adjustment for the August 26 meeting: each approved speaker could speak for a maximum of three minutes, and each Council member had three minutes to ask questions and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion. E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, A. Knack and A. Paquette voted in favour; none opposed. It carried 6–0. All six committee members appear in the attendance record, so 6/6 exceeds the two-thirds requirement.
citations.establishes: The carried meeting-wide reduction, its mover, terms, vote and sufficient committee support.

citations.finding: The item 2.3 Requests to Speak motion approved five panels for item 7.6 with 15, 15, 15, 15 and 4 entries. Reviewer calculation: 15+15+15+15+4=64. Fifteen entries carry an organization: panel counts 2, 8, 3, 2 and 0. The organizations named are Edmonton Bike Coalition, YEG Bike Coalition, Bike Bus Alberta, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, Paths for People, Ward Métis Bikes, Let's Bike There YEG and Bike Edmonton.
citations.establishes: The primary approved-entry count, within both stipulated bands; organization names do not establish speakers' positions.

citations.finding: Item 7.6 records four presentation panels with 16, 16, 16 and 2 public-speaker entries. Reviewer calculation: 16+16+16+2=50. If 'queue' is interpreted as those recorded as presenting, 50 falls below the primary 60–80 band, though it is inside the alternative 50–90 band.
citations.establishes: A materially different count under the required alternative definition, without undermining the primary approved-entry count.

items.title: Edmonton bike lane expansion to continue as planned (CBC, via Yahoo News Canada)

citations.finding: A CBC report republished on Yahoo describes 'dozens of cyclists' speaking at an infrastructure committee meeting. It gives no count and does not mention time limits.
citations.establishes: Only that a large number of speakers was reported. It establishes no count and nothing about the time limit.
citations.quote: Dozens of cyclists made their case to councillors at an infrastructure committee meeting

items.title: Infrastructure Committee, August 26, 2026, agenda page and minutes item 1.4
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Office of the City Clerk

citations.finding: The carried agenda page shows the scheduled adjournment as 5 p.m. The Orders of the Day motion under 1.4 moved adjournment to 9 p.m. Neither item records any reason for the speaker time-limit motion.
citations.establishes: Nothing about why the cut was made. The holder's stated reason (volume of complaints) is untested and is not supported by any City record identified.
